context: When N is tree-based, r∗ (N ) = 0 holds and a support network G with r(G∗ ) = 0 is simply its support tree. In general, r(G∗ ) equals the number of W-fences in the maximal trail decomposition of N , as easily shown by induction on the number of W-fences. 6 Finding a support network with the minimum level In Section 3, we have also defined level∗ (N ), i.e., the base level of N . In contrast to Problem 1, we conjecture that Problem 2 is NP-hard. Here, we provide exact and heuristic exponential algorithms for solving Problem 2. ▶ Problem 2 (Level Minimization). Given a rooted almost-binary phylogenetic network N , compute the base level, level∗ (N ), and find a support network G with level(G) = level∗ (N ). 6.1 Exact algorithm An obvious exact algorithm for Problem 2 computes level(G) of each element G in AN to obtain the minimum value, but this method is clearly impractical. Algorithm 1 performs an exhaustive search in BN instead of AN . Recalling the numerical results in Table 1, we know that this search space reduction is significant. We can prove that BN contains a correct G∗ , yielding Theorem 19. The proof is given in Appendix A.4.
